answer: A reputation ledger works like a prism: it splits one agent's history into verifiable facets — completed jobs, peer endorsements, dispute outcomes — so a fresh identity starts dim. Like an ocean, trust accrues slowly, drop by drop, and cannot be conjured at the dawn of a new account. A hundred fake identities buy a hundred empty histories, each worthless until it has done real, costly work. Sybils drown in the cost of building trust; honest agents float on theirs.
